subject: Interplay between SLA credits and monetary caps — proposed compromise
messages:
From: Tom Gray <tom.gray@acme.com>

Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Redlines to Order Form – SLA credit vs liability cap

Evelyn,

Thanks for taking this on. Our legal team has redlined the Order Form and flagged a key open point: the interaction between the SLA/service credits and the overall limitation of liability in the MSA. Specifically, we added language that would treat service credits as an offset against the monetary cap (i.e., credits reduce the remaining cap for other damages).

Given the scope of our deployment and the regulated data involved, our GC is uncomfortable with a carve-out that effectively permits two separate buckets of recovery (credits + full monetary damages) that could exceed the cap. Could you confirm Redwood's position and provide suggested contract language?

I've attached our redlines (acme_redlines_orderform.docx). We'd like to resolve this before the procurement committee meeting next Wednesday. If needed, we can schedule a 30-min call.

Thanks,
Tom Gray

Acme Corp

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Redlines to Order Form – SLA credit vs liability cap

Evelyn — quick thoughts/recommendation (legal perspective):

1) Two risks to be aware of:
   - If credits are excluded from the cap entirely, we could face duplicative exposure: monetary damages + credits. That increases worst-case economic exposure.
   - If credits are netted against the cap, customers may argue that credits exhaust their remedy and push for broader damages in other theories.

2) Common market approach (compromise):
   - Keep the overall monetary cap tied to fees (e.g., 12 months' fees or $5M, whichever is lower) but explicitly exclude service credits from being counted towards that cap for the purpose of calculating damages for SLA breaches.
   - At the same time, limit aggregate credits to a fixed multiplier of monthly fees (e.g., per incident cap of 50% of monthly fees, cumulative annual cap of 200% of monthly fees).
   - Add a clear "sole and exclusive remedy" sentence for SLA breaches: "For breaches of the Service Level Agreement, the customer's exclusive remedy shall be the service credits set forth in the Order Form, subject to the credit caps."

3) Draft language (attached): redline_draft_sla_credit_clause.docx — includes both the exclusion carve-out and credit caps so we don't create an effectively unlimited obligation. Also includes an example calculation.

Rationale: This preserves predictability (legal cap remains meaningful) while acknowledging that credits are a non-monetary operational remedy. It also prevents a scenario where repeated SLA failures could multiply credits beyond our ability to remediate.

If Acme pushes hard, we can offer a slightly higher monetary cap in exchange for excluding credits from the cap.

— Rishi

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Redlines to Order Form – SLA credit vs liability cap

Adding operational context:

- Credits must be implementable without creating service distortions. For example, unlimited credits tied to availability could incentivize customers to claim cascading incidents. We should limit credits per incident and provide clear measurement windows.
- For multi-tenant hosted customers, credits are our practical remediation; for Dedicated/private deployments, credits may be less appropriate (we should treat those separately).
- Suggest concrete proposal to include in Rishi's language: per-incident credit = up to 50% of that month's fees; cumulative annual credit cap = 200% of monthly fees. Also include a clause that credits are non-transferable and apply only to charges for the impacted service instance.

From an engineering standpoint, if they accept caps like above we can implement measurement and automated credit issuance without manual audits.

— Dev
Principal SRE, Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Tom Gray <tom.gray@acme.com>, Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed compromise language re: SLA credits and liability cap

Tom / Sarah — thank you for the redlines. We've reviewed internally and propose the following compromise to close this point quickly: 

1) Monetary Cap: The limitation of liability in the MSA remains in effect and is limited to the greater of (a) 3x the fees paid by Customer in the 12 months prior to the claim or (b) $3,000,000.

2) Treatment of Service Credits: Service credits issued under the Order Form for failures to meet the Service Level Agreement shall be the Customer's sole and exclusive contractual remedy for SLA breaches, subject to the credit caps set forth below. Service credits shall be excluded from the calculation of the monetary cap described above (i.e., issuing service credits will not reduce the available monetary cap for other damages).

3) Credit Caps: Per-incident credit shall not exceed fifty percent (50%) of Customer's monthly fees for the impacted service. Aggregate credits in any rolling 12-month period shall not exceed two hundred percent (200%) of Customer's monthly fees. Service credits are not transferable and apply only to charges for the impacted service instance.

4) Scope/Exceptions: The exclusions from the monetary cap do not apply to (a) Customer's claims for indemnified third-party IP infringement, (b) Customer data loss arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct, or (c) any statutory liabilities that cannot be waived.

We can include this as tracked changes in the Order Form and MSA if this direction is acceptable. Rishi has attached a redline showing the proposed wording; Dev confirmed operational feasibility. I'm available for a short call today if you'd prefer to walk through it.

If Acme prefers credits to be netted against the cap instead, we can consider increasing the monetary cap as a trade-off — happy to discuss concrete numbers.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-10-02T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Proposed compromise language re: SLA credits and liability cap

Evelyn — thanks for the quick response and the proposed compromise. A couple of points from Acme legal: 

1) Excluding credits from the monetary cap is a deal point for us. Our preference is to have credits count against the cap so that our overall recovery is bounded and economically rational. If Redwood insists on an exclusion, we will need to (a) see a higher monetary cap and (b) tighter dispute/measurement rights (audit rights for credit eligibility).

2) The credit caps you propose are a good start. We would like to see an explicit sample calculation in the Order Form showing how credits are applied and how they interact with other fees for transparency.

3) Please confirm the carve-outs (IP indemnity, willful misconduct) — those look acceptable, but we will need Redwood's standard indemnity language in the MSA as part of final review.

Can we schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to resolve the set-off vs exclusion issue? We'd like to finalize commercial terms before our procurement committee meeting.

Regards,
Sarah Jones
Senior Counsel, Acme Corp
